# Numerical fixtures

`causal-convolutions.json` uses CPU PyTorch 2.14.1, `torch.manual_seed(42)`:
random input `(1,2,7)`, transpose weights `(2,3,6)`, bias `(3)`;
`conv_transpose1d(stride=3)` with the last three samples removed. The next
random input `(1,2,19)`, depthwise weights `(2,1,7)` and bias `(2)` use
18 samples of left padding, dilation 3 and two groups.

`tokenizer.json` uses SentencePiece 0.2.2 BPE reconstructed from the pinned
production GGUF's pieces, scores and types, byte fallback and identity
normalization. It adds the dummy whitespace prefix, preserves repeated
whitespace, and applies the official merged-Chinese-token expansion.
`tools/tts/voxcpm_tokenizer_reference.py` revalidates these IDs by calling
`mask_multichar_chinese_tokens` directly from the pinned official source.
Only U+4E00..U+9FFF pieces present as plain multi-character vocabulary entries
are expanded, matching that wrapper rather than extending its Unicode policy.

`original-tokenizer.json` instead uses the actual `LlamaTokenizerFast` loaded
from official weight revision 32279effe8c19989596f05d353d1447f51d9e915,
with that same pinned model wrapper. Three of the 17 inputs differ from the
GGUF/SentencePiece fixtures; do not rewrite one fixture set to hide the other.
The Rust original-weight path uses Hugging Face BPE and matches all 17 IDs.

Real-weight intermediate tensors are generated by
`tools/tts/voxcpm_reference.py` from the pinned official source, not checked
into Git. Opt-in Rust tests use `VOXCPM_TEST_MODELS` and
`VOXCPM_TEST_REFERENCE`. All F32 assertions retain atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4.

For original weights, pass `--original-models ORIGINAL_DIRECTORY` to the
oracle script, keeping `--gguf-python` as the pinned mapping reference. Run
the Rust oracle with `VOXCPM_ORACLE_ORIGINAL=1`, `VOXCPM_TEST_MODELS` pointing
at the original assets and `VOXCPM_TEST_REFERENCE` at the new oracle directory.
